children: LVMH (MC) fell 2.59% in Paris after HSBC downgraded it to Hold from Buy. The bank cut its LVMH target to 490 from 600, and raised its sector beta to 1.10 from 1.00. Analysts led by Anne-Laure Bismuth wrote that "H2 2026 won't get any rosier and could prove more difficult to navigate."

Organic sales growth across HSBC's luxury coverage reached 7.0% in the second quarter against 5.8% in the first, helped by jewellery demand and better traffic in the U.S. and Asia. The problem is the comparison base, alongside softer mainland China sentiment and social media backlash over an intellectual property dispute involving a Chinese tea brand.

For LVMH, Fashion and Leather generated 72% of group EBIT in 2025 and faces a slow recovery, with Louis Vuitton at roughly 20 billion in sales finding growth harder to come by. Dior's turnaround under Jonathan Anderson is progressing gradually.

HSBC also downgraded Burberry to Hold from Buy and cut its price target to 1,200 pence from 1,350, lifting its weighted average cost of capital assumption to 9.9% from 9.4% on the higher sector beta. The bank credits Josh Schulman with a turnaround that has lifted the shares about 51% since November 2024, but sees limited scope for upward revisions and notes the company must accelerate sharply against a two-year China sales stack over the next three quarters. HSBC kept Buy ratings on Richemont, Kering, Moncler and Prada, with Richemont its preferred name on the view that hard luxury keeps beating soft.

title: HSBC Cuts LVMH as Luxury's Second Half Won't Get Any Rosier
